newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER WOODS WINS SI'S SPORTSMAN OF YEAR HONOR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER WOODS WINS SI'S SPORTSMAN OF YEAR HONOR.

text.p: Tiger Woods, who has taken the golf world by storm at the age of 20, was named Tuesday the 1996 Sports Illustrated Sportsman of the Year.

Woods, whose given name is Eldrick, won an unprecedented third consecutive United States Amateur Championship in August. The long-hitting Woods then turned professional and stunned the tour with two victories in his first seven starts.
Woods, who is part black and part Thai and has stirred minority interest in golf, also won the NCAA Championship college title this season while a Stanford student.
"Our selection of Tiger is not based on the assumption that he's going to win countless major championships," said the magazine's managing editor Bill Colson in presenting the award.

"In my mind, he doesn't have to win another tournament to be a most deserving Sportsman of the Year. His game, his dramatic victories, his competitive nature and his enormous impact on the sport, both on and off the golf course, make him a compelling selection..."
The spectacular arrival on tour of Woods, whose long-hitting and charisma have made him a huge gallery favourite, has been the biggest thing to hit golf since Jack Nicklaus turned pro in 1962.

Woods, who launched his pro career with a five-year endorsement deal with NIKE worth a reported $40 million, finished 24th on the U.S. money list with $790,594 from eight events and already is 14th in the Ryder Cup standings.

In addition to his tour money, Woods also won $40,000 in the Skins contest with John Daly, Fred Couples and Tom Watson and had a $75,577 payday with Kelli Kuhene for being runner-up in the JCPenney Classic.

Woods first picked up a golf club at six months old. His last U.S. Amateur championship ran his streak of winning U.S. national titles to six seasons in a row following his junior successes -- a feat matched only by the legendary Bobby Jones.
